title: The radio at work said my name at 3 🎙️
style_prompt: dark blue cinematic night, faceless silhouette, fog, minimal interior, no text, no watermark
hook_text: At 3:00 in the morning the radio at my night shift said my name, and then my address.

scenes.narration: At 3:00 in the morning the radio at my night shift said my name, and then my address.
I stack shelves in a warehouse on my own. The old radio on the office shelf has been dead for years. The wire is coiled up beside it.
But it was playing. Static, then a calm presenter's voice, reading the late news. Tonight's top story, he said, a man named after me is working alone.
He read my street. He read my flat number. He read what I had for dinner, and where I had left my keys, in the pocket of my work jacket.
I looked behind the radio. No wire, no battery, nothing. The static swelled and the voice said, and now the weather outside the warehouse.
Light rain, it said. A strong wind. And a person standing at the loading door, in a grey coat, with a torch, waiting for the night worker to come out.
I went to the loading door and looked through the glass. A figure stood in the rain, in a grey coat, holding a torch, as still as a post.
The radio crackled one last time. And the presenter said, that is all for tonight. The man outside walks in when you stop listening.
So tell me. Do you switch the radio off, or keep listening?
